\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ختم} (khatm)}{ختم (khatm)}]{\fa{ختم} (khatm) — a memorial gathering}

\label{lesson:FA-C338-khatm}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to bury, then the Persian for a grave.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ختم}}
\textbf{\fa{ختم}} (\emph{khatm}) — \textquotedblleft{}a memorial gathering\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مراسم} \fa{ختم} \fa{در} \fa{مسجد} \fa{برگزار} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Marâsem-e khatm dar masjed bargozâr shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The memorial service was held at the mosque.
\end{quote}

A gathering soon after a death, often at a mosque. \emph{khatm} first means \textquotedblleft{}a completion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khatm} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{khatm}, \textquotedblleft{}a sealing, a completion\textquotedblright{}, as of a reading of the Quran for the dead. EtymDB lists the Persian word with no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khatm}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khatm}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khatm}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to bury, then the Persian for a grave, then say \emph{khatm} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عزا} ('azâ)}{عزا ('azâ)}]{\fa{عزا} ('azâ) — mourning}

\label{lesson:FA-C338-aza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a grave, then the Persian for a memorial gathering.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عزا}}
\textbf{\fa{عزا}} (\emph{'azâ}) — \textquotedblleft{}mourning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خانواده} \fa{یک} \fa{هفته} \fa{عزا} \fa{داشتند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khânevâde yek hafte 'azâ dâshtand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The family were in mourning for a week.
\end{quote}

\emph{'Azâdâr} \textquotedblleft{}a mourner\textquotedblright{}; black clothes are worn in \emph{'azâ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'azâ} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{'azā'}, \textquotedblleft{}solace, mourning\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تسلیت} \fa{گفتن} (tasliyat goftan)}{تسلیت گفتن (tasliyat goftan)}]{\fa{تسلیت} \fa{گفتن} (tasliyat goftan) — to offer condolences}

\label{lesson:FA-C338-tasliyat-goftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a memorial gathering, then the Persian for mourning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تسلیت} \fa{گفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{تسلیت} \fa{گفتن}} (\emph{tasliyat goftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to offer condolences\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{همه} \fa{همکاران} \fa{به} \fa{او} \fa{تسلیت} \fa{گفتند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hame-ye hamkârân be u tasliyat goftand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
All his colleagues offered him their condolences.
\end{quote}

The person takes \emph{be}. Present stem \emph{gu-}: \emph{tasliyat miguyam}, in speech \emph{tasliyat migam} \textquotedblleft{}my condolences\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tasliyat} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{tasliya}, \textquotedblleft{}consolation\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{goftan} \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{} is native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasliyat goftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tasliyat goftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a memorial gathering, then the Persian for mourning, then say \emph{tasliyat goftan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{وصیت} (vasiyat)}{وصیت (vasiyat)}]{\fa{وصیت} (vasiyat) — a will, a last wish}

\label{lesson:FA-C338-vasiyat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for mourning, then the Persian for to offer condolences.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{وصیت}}
\textbf{\fa{وصیت}} (\emph{vasiyat}) — \textquotedblleft{}a will, a last wish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{وصیت} \fa{خود} \fa{خانه} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{دخترش} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar vasiyat-e khod khâne râ be dokhtarash dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In his will he left the house to his daughter.
\end{quote}

\emph{Vasiyatnâme} is a written will.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vasiyat} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{waṣiyya} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), usually glossed \textquotedblleft{}a bequest, a last instruction\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ارث} (ers)}{ارث (ers)}]{\fa{ارث} (ers) — an inheritance}

\label{lesson:FA-C338-ers}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to offer condolences, then the Persian for a will.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ارث}}
\textbf{\fa{ارث}} (\emph{ers}) — \textquotedblleft{}an inheritance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{فرش} \fa{از} \fa{مادربزرگم} \fa{به} \fa{ارث} \fa{رسیده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In farsh az mâdarbozorgam be ers reside ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This carpet came down to me from my grandmother.
\end{quote}

Written with \fa{ث}. \emph{Be ers residan} \textquotedblleft{}to be inherited\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ers} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{irth}, \textquotedblleft{}inheritance\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
